items.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021
items.q: I liked Charles Lloyd “Live at Monterey” that was another classic on Atlantic with Keith Jarrett on piano, a young Keith Jarrett.

ctx.x: But in Sun Ra’s case, do you think he would have appealed to more listeners if his mythology and his clothing and his whole persona — I’m trying to form this question.

If he had toned it down I don’t think he would have been more popular. Because he would not be able to do that. This was a total hypothetical. Part of the thrill of going to see Sun Ra was his unpredictability. One time you go there and he leads everybody out into the streets like the Pied Piper and the entire audience followed him, followed behind him. And he took them around the block of the venue and then back and you know, into the venue, and everyone took their seats. It was exhilarating. Another time there…
Did you ever get a sense of what it was like at Sun Ra’s home and place of rehearsal? Did any of his members ever describe that to you?
